topic: What frequency planning challenges arise when coordinating multiple ground stations with overlapping satellite visibility windows?
consensus_response: When coordinating multiple ground stations with overlapping satellite visibility windows, frequency planning challenges arise due to potential interference between satellite and terrestrial networks. This interference can lead to a decrease in signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), reducing the array factor of the ground stations' antennas. The increasing number of satellites and terrestrial networks operating on the same frequencies exacerbates this issue, necessitating tight coordination between networks. This coordination can be achieved through Adaptive Frequency Hopping (AFH), but it introduces additional complexity and latency, impacting system performance and capacity. Proper frequency planning and coordination are essential to mitigate these challenges and maintain spectral efficiency.
